key_insight: In renewables-rich distribution grids, local electricity markets can lower customer and system costs under uncertainty, but the value of batteries depends strongly on where they sit relative to PV and load.
engineering_relevance: For distribution planners, the study shows that market design and storage siting must be co-optimized with PV growth to avoid congestion and unlock grid value.
method: Model PV inflow as an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process to capture uncertainty and temporal correlation.
Run rolling-horizon alternating optimal power flow on the IEEE 123-node feeder.
Compare flat tariff, real-time pricing, and local electricity market designs across PV and storage penetration levels.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports comparative evaluation of operator, customer, and system costs plus storage value on the IEEE 123-node feeder under uncertain PV and multiple market paradigms.
watch_item: Local electricity markets may worsen customer outcomes at very low PV penetration, so adoption should be timed with PV expansion and careful storage deployment.
paper_title: Understanding the role and value of battery storage in renewables-rich distribution grids under uncertainty and different market paradigms
